name: OpenVibe.Zone

liveness.means: the process is up and answers HTTP; the database is what ready checks

resumes.what: sign-in sessions are cookies verified against Network's keys, fetched again at boot
every zone is a committed row with a revision; a zone still provisioning, or deleting, is pushed to Media again (Media applies only a higher revision)
the deletion poller resumes every zone in state deleting and marks it deleted once Media reports nothing left

conditions: automatic: ovhost deploy puts the previous sha back and restarts again when the ready URL does not answer 2xx within ready.timeoutSeconds after the restart (exit 3)
rollback.window: automatic only while ovhost waits for readiness after the restart; manual afterwards, as long as no blocker applies

blockers.none: migration 0001 only creates Zone's own tables; Media keeps serving every zone from its projection while Zone is down

leases.none: no claims: one process serves the site, the API and the deletion poller

notes: Port 5050, unit openvibe-zone.service, openvibe.zone (its own certificate; api.openvibe.zone waits for its DNS record). Named object zones per project environment (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): Zone owns the zone record, its name (never reused), state, quota setting and control API in its own PostgreSQL database (ov_zone, ADR-035), and provisions every change in OpenVibe.Media, which owns the objects, bytes, replicas, the S3 and native data APIs, quota enforcement, usage counting, the access keys and the one deletion path. Zone never lists keys or holds bytes. Its site is the storage console: a project's zones, their usage, S3 access keys (issued by Media), and how to use them.

site.name: Zone
site.tagline: Private S3-compatible storage for your projects.
site.what: Named storage zones for each project and environment: buckets that the AWS SDKs, rclone and backup tools reach over S3, with access keys you scope to a zone and quotas you set.
